Fixes a safety rail that was silently disabled on 16:10 displays.

`_confirm_wall_upgrade` guards every wall purchase by looking for the buy-with-gems dialog, both before and after it clicks Okay — the check after the click is the last thing standing between an unaffordable confirm and a gem spend. Both checks were wrapped in "use this template if it exists", and `templates/16_10/needgold_x.png` does not ship. Template lookup resolves against the active aspect with no fallback, so on 16:10 the guard evaluated to absent and was skipped. On 16:9 it always worked.

- Refuse to confirm a wall upgrade at all when the gem-dialog template is missing for the active aspect, instead of clicking Okay unprotected.
- Skip the wall-upgrade cycle early in that case, with one error log and a status line explaining why, rather than running the ~30s open/scroll/add sequence and rejecting it at the end.
- Add a regression covering the refusal.

**If you run at 16:10, wall upgrades are now off** until `templates/16_10/needgold_x.png` is captured on a 16:10 client. That is the only missing piece; nothing else changes. Farming, auto-upgrade and Builder Base are unaffected, and 16:9 behaves exactly as before. A safety check that vanishes quietly is worse than a feature that stops loudly.

Download **BasePilot.exe**. Tesseract is bundled. **BasePilot.exe.sha256** contains its SHA-256 checksum. The exe is unsigned, so SmartScreen warns on first launch.

Validation is limited to the automated regressions and the build's startup smoke check. The wall-upgrade path has not been re-validated against a live game at either aspect.
